primitives.name: Left Half Decoy Trajectory
primitives.verbatim_quote: Left Half Back runs off right tackle with all appearances of having the ball.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: $\vec{v}_{LH}$: velocity vector of Left Half (m/s), $\hat{n}_{RT}$: normal vector of Right Tackle boundary (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Defensive agents assign non-zero probability mass to the visual trajectory of the Left Half.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the decoy velocity magnitude is insufficient to trigger a pursuit response from secondary defenders.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSI's 'Attention Sink' operator, measuring how effectively a dummy node absorbs adversarial computational resources.
layer2.telemetry: Distance traveled by nearest defensive back towards the Left Half.

primitives.name: Fullback Hesitation Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: 201 FOOTBALL Tackle Back Formation—Fake Attack—Full Back Buck on Left Side.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: $\Delta t_{hes}$: hesitation duration (s), $a_{FB}$: acceleration of Fullback ($m/s^2$)
primitives.assumptions: A brief pause in acceleration allows the offensive line's interference blocks to fully materialize and displace defenders.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs if $\Delta t_{hes}$ exceeds the reaction time threshold of the defensive line, resulting in immediate sack/tackle for loss.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's 'Phase-Lock Delay', optimizing the timing between offensive line displacement and ball-carrier entry into the gap.
layer2.telemetry: Time difference between snap and fullback's first step.

primitives.name: Rear Assist Momentum Transfer
primitives.verbatim_quote: Right End comes around and assists the runner from behind.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: $\vec{p}_{RE}$: momentum of Right End (kg m/s), $\vec{p}_{FB}$: momentum of Fullback (kg m/s)
primitives.assumptions: Conservation of momentum applies during the rear-assist collision; the Right End adds positive impulse to the Fullback's trajectory.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if the angle of incidence between the Right End and Fullback causes lateral deflection rather than forward propulsion.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's 'Vector Augmentation' primitive, calculating the net gain in yardage provided by trailing blockers.
layer2.telemetry: Change in Fullback's velocity post-contact with Right End.

Simultaneously, the left halfback executes a high-velocity decoy trajectory along the right tackle boundary, maximizing the visual entropy and stretching the defensive width. While the defense is computationally overloaded by these dual deceptions, the offensive line establishes an interference lattice. The fullback, acting as the primary eigenstate of the play, introduces a critical temporal delay ($\Delta t_{hes}$). This hesitation is not passive; it is a precise synchronization gate allowing the interference blocks to reach terminal velocity and displace their assigned defenders. Finally, the fullback penetrates through the left guard. The right end and right halfback wrap around, applying rearward momentum transfer to augment the fullback's penetration depth. The success of the primitive relies entirely on the orthogonality of the decoy vectors to the true penetration vector, ensuring maximal defensive misallocation.

They assume the defense relies heavily on short-horizon visual cues—specifically the quarterback's arm angle and the initial trajectory of the backfield runners. By exploiting these heuristics, the offense induces a cascading failure in the defense's decision tree. The defense is forced to treat the left halfback as a high-probability threat, thereby violating optimal resource allocation principles. The offense essentially hacks the defense's predictive coding, turning their reactive instincts into the very mechanism of their own defeat.
